summary.text: The Big Dipper, called the Plough in the UK and Ireland, is an asterism of seven bright stars in the constellation Ursa Major.
Four of its stars form a bowl or body and three form a handle or head.
A line through its two front stars, Merak and Dubhe, points to Polaris, the current northern pole star, which makes it useful in celestial navigation.

facts.label: The Pointers
facts.value: Merak and Dubhe, which point toward Polaris

facts.label: Parent constellation
facts.value: Ursa Major, Latin for Greater Bear

items.prompt: On a clear night you want to find Polaris, starting from the Big Dipper. What do you do?

options.label: Extend a line through the three stars of the handle
Follow a line from the dimmest star toward the horizon
Extend an imaginary line through its two front stars
Draw a line through the double star Mizar and Alcor

items.explain: Polaris can be located by extending an imaginary line through the front two stars, Merak and Dubhe.

items.prompt: Is the Big Dipper itself a constellation?

options.label: Yes, it is the whole of Ursa Major
No, it is an asterism of seven stars within Ursa Major
Yes, it is the Little Dipper's parent constellation
No, it is a single double star

items.explain: The Big Dipper is an asterism consisting of seven bright stars of the constellation Ursa Major.

items.prompt: People across Europe have seen the same seven stars as a bear, a wagon, a plough or a ladle. What does this show?

options.label: One star pattern can be read as many different things
Each name refers to a different group of stars
Only one of these readings can be correct
Ancient peoples could not see the stars clearly

items.explain: Ursa Major has been seen as a bear, a plough, a wagon, or a ladle, and many cultures gave the pattern their own names.

items.prompt: In Germanic languages the wagon name referred to the men's wagon. Which star pattern was the women's wagon?

options.label: The Seven Oxen
The Pointers
Odin's Wain
The Little Dipper

items.explain: The original reference was to the churls' (men's) wagon, in contrast to the women's wagon, the Little Dipper.

items.prompt: The famous double star Mizar and Alcor has another name tied to a team of animals. What is it?

options.label: The Plough and Ox
The Horse and Rider
The Bear and Cub
The Wagon and Driver

items.explain: The double star Mizar/Alcor is also called the Horse and Rider.

items.prompt: In one Arabic tradition, the Dipper's bowl and handle stars tell a story of mourning. What do the four bowl stars stand for?

options.label: A team of horses pulling a cart
A bear chased across the night sky
A funeral litter, called a bier
A net cast by a Finnish fisher

items.explain: The four bowl stars represent a funeral bier, while the three handle stars symbolize mourners or daughters following behind.
